articleTitle: Used Car Price Prediction using Machine Learning: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In many business fields that are related to statistics and machine learning (ML), multiple linear regression (MLR) models are often used to estimate and fit a linear relationship between a continuous response variable and other explanatory variables. In our case study, we applied several regression techniques based on supervised machine learning to predict the resale price of used cars given many factors such as mileage, fuel type, fiscal power, mark, model, and the production year of the car. In all tested models, gradient boosting regressor showed a high R-squared score and low root mean square error.

articleTitle: Automatic detection of Moroccan coastal upwelling from chlorophyll-a concentration images using the Expectation-Maximization method
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The inshore water along the Atlantic coast of Morocco is part of one of the four major upwelling systems in the world. This region is characterized by the presence of upwelling activity almost all years around. In this work, we propose an unsupervised algorithm for identifying and extracting automatically this vital zone using the satellite observation of chlorophyll-a concentration (CHL-a). In fact, the approach is started with the application of Expectation-Maximisation algorithm for detecting the nutrient-rich region over CHL-a image. Then, a region-growing algorithm is applied to remove the noisy structures appeared in the offshore waters not belonging to the upwelling region. The proposed methodology is tested over a database of 230 weekly CHL-a images spanning the period from the years 2016 to 2020. The results show that the proposed method seems to be applicable for any other ecosystem.

articleTitle: Predicting smart grid stability using machine learning algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) allows applications to become more accurate at predicting outcome using data as inputs to predict output values, there are multiple models providing different results and each of them represents a complement of the other models with a principal goal that is the improvement of the prediction performances, ML is applied in various fields to give good predictions and allow to take the right actions depending on the subject. The current paper represents a case study of ML models use in order to predict the smart grid stability to forecast problems that can occur in the grid when renewable energy is used and electricity’s production is not sufficient to meet the consumer’s needs. This study is based on the “Electrical Grid Stability Simulated Dataset” provided by the Karlsruher Institut für Technologie, that have been preprocessed and used by various ML models. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) model allowed to have better results and reached an accuracy of 95.23% using f_classif features selection technique.

articleTitle: Randomized Tensor Singular Value Decomposition for Multidimensional Data Compression
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: We propose in this paper a randomized tensor singular value decomposition (SVD) based on tensor product. The SVD is widely used in literature as reduction data method. Its randomized matrix version is an attractive method for computing low-rank matrix approximation. Motivated by the tensor SVD approach recently proposed in many works and by the effectiveness of randomized approaches, we present a randomized tensor SVD. We extend the well-known randomized matrix factorization to tensors showing their effectiveness. A modified randomized tensor SVD is presented. Both theoretical results and numerical examples are provided to illustrate the performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Application of Paired Samples t-Test in Engineering Service-Learning Project
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: This paper presents the application in engineering education of Paired Samples t-Test statistical technique. The targeted application is the evaluation of Smile project, which takes place every year and implements a new engineering learning approach, the Engineering Service-Learning. The considered edition is the one of 2019, in which two teams of five engineering students each from Chouaib Doukkali University (Morocco) and Pusan National University (South Korean) participated. The Paired Samples t-Test allowed to check the initial state and to evaluate the evolution of participants’ skills and competencies.

articleTitle: Real-time Traffic Data Collection Using The Two Simulators SUMO and OMNeT++
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are one of the encouraging solutions to improve energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions in the transportation sector. Today, electric vehicles have experienced massive growth that has brought multiple benefits to the energy and transportation sectors, but they can also affect the stability of the smart grid, consuming more energy, especially during peak hours. In such deployments, energy efficiency and optimal energy distribution are among the most important constraints to be considered, to meet the energy demand of the electric vehicle. Indeed, traffic conditions have an impact on the energy consumption of electric vehicles. In this regard, it is essential to have real-time information on the traffic elements that offer flexibility in the management of the load. Faced with this challenge, the ITS-G5 technology is a promising solution that allows us to collect and transmit efficiently the traffic information in real-time and for this purpose, our work is validated by the two simulators SUMO and OMNeT++.

articleTitle: An optimisation solution of Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP)
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Nowadays, the continuous increase in traffic makes the management of road flows increasingly difficult. Hence, transportation network and delivery problems are becoming a real priority. To solve this complexity of situation we call on Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP). When we have capacity constraints, we talk about Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) considered as a variant of Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP). Due to the increasing of supply chain complexity, new optimization techniques in additional to new technologies give a great development, and so new Information and Communications Technologies (ICT) are implemented as support to the transportation and logistics management. This paper develops an optimization algorithm to solve CVRP of goods. We give an example of delivery distribution of BIM Stores in El Jadida city in Morocco. The aim is to deliver goods to the different points of Bim stores for a minimum cost while never exceeding the capacity of trucks to optimize the trucks tour. For that, we use an algorithm of operational research using Python language: The Guided Local Search. The results obtained represent the optimal path for delivering goods to different points of BIM stores in El Jadida city.

articleTitle: Human Action Recognition Using Squeezed Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In recent years, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) gained great success in many applications, especially in computer vision. In this paper we propose a novel deep learning approach for Human Action Recognition inspired by one of the most popular architectures being SqueezeNet with an incredibly small model size. The results show that the proposed model performs well on a KTH dataset as well as UCF-Sport dataset

articleTitle: Pain Detection From Facial Expressions Based on Transformers and Distillation
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Pain assessment is a challenging problem in the field of emotion recognition. Pain represents a complex emotion difficult to detect or to estimate its intensity. This is what makes automatic pain assessment playing an important role in clinical diagnosis. Taking into consideration that pain generally generates spontaneous facial behaviour, these facial expressions could be used to detect the presence of pain. As a matter of fact, previous researches used machine learning and deep learning either to detect pain or to estimate pain level. In this paper, we propose a fine-tuning of pre-trained data-efficient image transformers and distillation (Deit) for pain detection from facial expressions. The effectiveness of the proposed architecture is evaluated on two publicly available databases, namely UNBC McMaster Shoulder Pain and BioVid Heat Pain. The proposed approach achieved promising preliminary results compared to the state of the art.

articleTitle: Adaptive Region Growing based on detecting the seed point in the central trachea to the pre-segment respiratory system
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: This work proposes an efficient and valuable respiratory system pre-segmentation method from computed tomography (CT) images for medical software. The aim is to improve the efficiency of lung cancer treatment, early pulmonary nodule detection, and help for COVID 19 diagnostics. The proposed approach starts with looking for (in a specific range of Hounsfield pixel values) the center of the best area of the central trachea, this will serve as a seed point for a 3D region growing to pre-segment lung and trachea. Our approach has approved its effectiveness for respiratory system pre-segmentation and does not require any image preprocessing algorithms. For a dataset of 70 series (different patients) of a thoracic image, the method pre-segments the respiratory system in very remarkable durations with an average of 71,86 milliseconds for detecting the seed point and an average of about 40,69 seconds for the pre-segmentation of the respiratory system.Our experience shows that our algorithm can automatically pre-segment the respiratory system in a short time, and this work is easily scalable to become a fully automatic approach for lung and trachea segmentation.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of Mono-DSSH network topology of energy harvesting optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: This paper is a mathematical improvement of present electricity harvesting circuits and DSSH (Double Synchronized switch harvesting) methods for piezoelectric energy. We supply a hierarchical presentation primarily based on useful evaluation to distinguish between present options that may additionally show up comparable in look however flip out to be very distinct in practice. Based on this hierarchical presentation, definitions of topologies, architectures and strategies are given to keep away from redundancy between current and future solutions. Then, after a thorough and unified mathematical evaluation of the regularly occurring hassle to be addressed, we exhibit the types of the equations received as a feature of the numbers of fabric piezoelectric factors n and the coefficient $\beta$. In addition, we can see that the voltage consequently fashioned is in section with the velocity, and additionally the independence of the load with the frequency for this reason including a viscous friction impact to dampen the vibrations.

articleTitle: Vehicle speed measurement, type, and color identification by video processing using machine learning algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Every year many people lose their lives due to road accidents, mentioning that speed is the principal cause of this disaster, hence the need to control the vehicle’s speed. In this study, we intend to develop a video processing model by integrating cameras in the transportation sector to control vehicle traffic speed. This technique allows us to monitor traffic in real-time, quantify the traffic flow, and estimate the vehicle speed. Therefore, we will contribute to road safety improvement motivated by an unwavering desire to expect a reduction in road casualties. In this paper, we will implement machine learning algorithms to measure the vehicle’s velocity and identify its color and its type. Several tests were carried out to verify the model’s accuracy. According to the results obtained, the realized model operates successfully.

articleTitle: Lyapunov Design Controllers for Different Moments of Structured Cell Population Balance Model With Input Constraints
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In this work, we present a three nonlinear constrained control schemes, with an adjustable parameter, based on the Lyapunov design approach to regulate the different moments for a class of cell population balance model. The model consists of a partial integro-differential equation, describing cell growth, and an ordinary integro-differential equation, accounting for substrate consumption. A numerical simulation is presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Modeling of the effect of surfactant addition on electrolyte degradation in supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: This study describes for the first time the degradation of an organic electrolyte used in an activated carbon-based supercapacitor both with and without the presence of a surfactant. Decomposition reaction, which is considered as the major aging reaction of the supercapacitor, was studied by simulation by using a multiphysics finite element program. The obtained results clearly showed for both cases (presence and absence of surfactant) the production of a gas resulting from the electrolyte decomposition reaction, but with a higher rate without surfactant. In addition, the evolution of the concentration of the products of the degradation reaction with time appears to be less significant in the presence of surfactant than in the absence, indicating a significant effect of this element on reducing the aging time.

articleTitle: Stochastic Volatility, a closed formula for futures contracts
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Through this article, we have proposed a model for the variations of the spot price and volatility; we defined futures price as only a function of spot and volatility. Assuming that the market is complete, we induce the model to switch to the risk neutral universe, to benefit from the property which states that Futures contracts are martingales under the risk neutral probability. We obtain then a partial differential equation (PDE) verified by Futures price. By assuming that this same price is an affine function of both spot and volatility processes, we show that the term structure of the futures price is affine and we obtain a closed formula for futures contract which is the main result of this paper. We estimate afterward the parameters using an econometrics approach along with the likelihood method. However the accuracy of the method appears in the final result of the model as far as the market is concerned.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model for the Determination of The Young’s Modulus of Polyurethane (PU) and Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) Hearing Protectors
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Personal hearing protectors are tools that improve the conditions of workers. In order to study their efficiency and decrease the hearing lose. A finite elements method is presented in this work in order to give a physical characterization of hearing protectors materials. In harmony with the simplified model of Sessler [1] and for a better understanding of the studied materials behavior, we present in this work a new analytical model based on the assumption of the regular pores distribution in the polymer material. Given the scarcity of studies reporting the mechanical behavior of foams as a function of pore distribution and given that theoretical models do not predict any dependence of Young’s modulus with pore distribution and pore size, The aim of this work will be to determine the expression of Young’s modulus as a function of material parameters and matrix properties. These parameters will be used in the modeling of the mechanical behavior of a porous polymers sample based on polyurethane (PU) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC). This behavior model which depends on porosity and other factors affecting the porous character will allow to determine the sound absorption, transmission and reflection coefficients. It is important to mention that the theoretical value of Young’s modulus is based on the assumptions of elasticity theory.

articleTitle: Cooling system using several nanofluids
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Photovoltaic collector (PV) is a system that absorbs solar energy and convert it into electrical energy, due to the increase in temperature of the photovoltaic collectors (PV), and the heat loss is reduced, Our objective is to use a nanofluid that circulates under the solar panel and behaves as a heat exchanger, this study consists of a numerical modeling using computer software to compare the thermophysical properties of three nanofluids containing spherical nanoparticles of metal oxide type; TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and CuO which are dispersed in a base fluid; Ethylene glycol (EG) with a volume fraction from 0 to 3% and a constant nanoparticle diameter.

articleTitle: Optimal mass transportation for noise minimization problem around an airport
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In this article, we develop, for a given aircraft,a new optimization model based on optimal mass transportation to minimize the noise perceived on the ground. We make an application for the airport of DIASS (Senegal) taking into account the constraint known as the mass conservation equation (one of Euler’s equations). The problem is solved using an augmented Lagrangian algorithm introduced by Fortin [1]. Scenario simulations are carried out to illustrate that the sound level is decreasing, while the range and capacity of jets continue to increase.

articleTitle: An Image Fusion Method using Shift-invariant Adaptive Selectivity Representation and Parameter-Adaptive PCNN
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method for image fusion, which combines an adaptive selectivity representation with parameter-adaptive pulse-coupled neural network (PAPCNN). First, it uses a shift invariance multiscale and multiselective decomposition to capture the different geometric structures of source images, and to reduce the pseudo-Gibbs phenomena around singularities. Secondly, the multiscale-multiselective subbands are fused using PA-PCNN. Finally, the fused image is built based on an adaptive selectivity reconstruction, which enables more information from the source images to be retained. The experimental results elucidate that the proposed image fusion method is very effective in multifocus image fusion and infrared/visible Image.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing for Healthcare Services: Technology, Application and Architecture
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Cloud computing in healthcare becomes a growing field for improvement. The advent of cloud technology provides efficient and reliable outcomes to support healthcare services. Cloud technology reduces these costs for consumers and IT by improving clinical outcomes and quality of service for patients. Cloud technologies offer some of the best solutions for providing better medical services that easily and securely store and share medical information to improve operational efficiency and streamline costs for healthcare organizations. This article discusses the potential rule of cloud technology in healthcare, this may help to enhance the global healthcare scenario. Moreover, it presents the proposed architecture for healthcare services which is based on cloud computing.

articleTitle: Efficient mobility modeling of autonomous movement planning trajectories using AI algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The path planning plays an important role for autonomous systems. Efficient comprehension of the surrounding environment and the effective generation of an optimal collision-free path are two essential elements to resolve a path planning problem. Artificial intelligence permits solving issues related to path planning, where several algorithms are currently implemented for this purpose. In this work, we will consider analytically and theoretically four AI algorithms, namely: RRT, RRT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>, Q-Learning and GAN. We will demonstrate the different parameters affecting each algorithm to finally perform a performance analysis for various optimization metrics like execution time through simulation based experiments. Besides implementing each algorithm, we present a reliable contribution of parameters by exploring new environments to give a mobile node fixed trajectories for independent and autonomous mobilities.

articleTitle: Application of double exponential Sinc collocation method for the energy levels of the three-dimensional Schrödinger equation
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The energy levels of the time-independent Schrödinger equation are computed in three dimensions by applying double exponential Sinc collocation method. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the high accuracy of the proposed approach for different potential functions. Comparative tests with the single exponential Sinc collocation method are made to confirm the superiority of the double exponential Sinc collocation method.

articleTitle: Unsupervised image segmentation using Fuzzy Hidden Markov Chain with bi-dimensional data
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: This work deals with a method based on a fuzzy hidden Markov chain with bi-dimensional data for unsupervised segmentation of fuzzy images. Often, to apply the hidden Markov chain model on image segmentation we use a curve like Hilbert-Peano scan to transform a 2 D image to 1 D. The main characteristic of our approach is using it as an alternative of Hilbert-Peano scan and to treat the coexistence of hard and fuzzy pixels in the same image. We use the EM algorithm in bi-dimensional version (EM2D) for estimation of parameters in this model. We test the EM2D algorithm with the EM in one-dimensional case (EMID) with Hilbert-Peano scan by examining some criteria as segmentation quality and the error rate. The segmentation results demonstrate the quality of our model.

articleTitle: A stochastic 3D model for three-phase heterogeneous microstructures in SOFC-electrodes
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: An original stochastic model to simulate complex 3D microstructures of SOFC-electrodes with gradient and global heterogeneity has been developed. The synthetic microstructures generated by the model were compared to real microstructures of Ni-YSZ electrodes acquired by tomography. The ability of the model to generate representative microstructures has been demonstrated. Finally, the model was fitted on real electrode reconstructions. The results obtained shown that the phase surface area density curves and several microstructural properties of the synthetic microstructures were very close to those of the real ones. The flexibility of the model and the results obtained shown that it could be used in the framework of numerical microstructural optimizations of SOFC-electrodes.

articleTitle: Bilinear optimal stabilization of a non-homogeneous Fokker-Planck equation
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In this work, we study the bilinear optimal stabilization of a non-homogeneous Fokker-Planck equation. We first study the problem of optimal control in a finite-time interval and then focus on the case of the infinite time horizon. We further show that the obtained optimal control guarantees the strong stability of the system at hand. An illustrating numerical example is given.

articleTitle: Understanding changes in the structure of complex networks using QSAR/QSPR
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The Quantitative Structure-Activity/Property Relationships (QSAR/QSPR) models have been used, for many years, to solve different kinds of problems in different domains, such as mathematics, science, and chemistry. The classification-based QSAR/QSPR models represent an important study to predict and understand the changes in complex networks. In this context, the QSAR/QSPR use molecular descriptors as tools to represent and characterize the structure of networks. On the other hand, Complex Networks are useful in analyzing real-world networks which are all around us in chemistry, industry, mathematics, etc. These systems have topological characteristics that don’t appear in simple networks. We can cite, for instance, chemical networks, Technological networks, Biological networks, social networks. Indeed, complex networks have the same representation: vertices (atoms, routers, computers, pages, persons, etc) and edges (chemical bonds, physical links, friendship). To model and understand the changes and relationship between the components in these systems we use numeric parameters called Topological indices that allow us to describe the nature and the connectivity between the entities that represent the complex networks. The goal of this work is to use the topological indices to measure social network analysis by representing the accounts (persons) as vertices and the relationship between them as edge. In this paper, we are going to calculate distance-degree based topological index called the Degree Distance index DD(G) for some particular complex networks connected to each other in different ways.

articleTitle: Partial finite-time stabilization for a mono-dimensional transport bilinear system
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: This paper investigates the partial finite-time stabilization for a mono-dimensional transport equation using bilinear feedback control. We will first discuss the well-posedness of the system in closed-loop and then proceed to the question of partial stability at a settling time that depends on the initial state. The case of a prescribed time, using time-varying feedback, is discussed as well. Our approaches are based on the theory of maximal monotone nonlinear operators and the Lyapunov method.

articleTitle: Ensemble learning methods for deep learning: Application to skin lesions classification
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Despite all the contributions of deep learning (DL) which have contributed to improving performance in the field of dermatology, the classification of skin diseases remains challenging. Indeed, deep learning has made a great advancement in the field of medicine and has had the potential to improve practice in this field, from diagnosis to personalized treatment. However, it is not always relevant for certain issues, the performance of a single DL model is not always satisfactory. Ensemble approaches have proven their effectiveness in solving many Deep Learning challenges such as the classification task, as well, the accuracy of the final prediction process can be improved by training many models and combining them. In this paper, the ensemble learning approach is explored by combining several architectures in order to detect and classify benign and malignant skin cancer diseases. The results obtained demonstrate the usefulness of this approach in the classification of skin cancer images, ensemble model achieved an accuracy rate 0.96 of and AUC score of 0.96.

articleTitle: Disaster Assessment in Humanitarian Relief Supply Chain: Application to the Moroccan context
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop and apply a new approach of disaster management which combine risk management tools with disaster management process in order to determine the critical disasters using the criticality as an indicator of evaluation in order to extract the disaster classes and recommend possible solutions. The implementation of the approach in Moroccan context as a case study prove the effectiveness of the model as a decision-making tool.

articleTitle: A new classification model with a multi-layer dimensionality reduction approach
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Documents categorization has evolved into a pertinent study topic, adding new challenges to data mining and information retrieval fields. However, classification algorithms suffer from the large sparse matrix generated from the processed dataset. Therefore, reducing data dimensionality is considered an essential phase in the whole process of classification. This phase aims to remove irrelevant features while enhancing the classifier’s performance. Several feature extraction and selection methods have been introduced and discussed. Still, applying these methods in Arabic topic categorization is not well-studied and left behind in comparison with various languages like English. In this paper, we highlight the benefit of using a hybrid multi-layer dimension reduction approach, especially for Arabic topic classification. The procedure proposed includes four layers of feature extraction and selection. The first two layers apply linguistic methods, while the last two layers use statistical analyses. Then, a bagging classifier model is implemented using the Support Vector Machines (SVM) as its base model. Finally, we evaluated the classifier performance using several measurable criteria such as precision, recall, accuracy, and F-score. According to the literature, the presented model reached an average accuracy that is among the best results reported in previous studies.

articleTitle: Terrestrial Connectivity Through Constellations of High Altitude Platform Station (HAPS)
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: A High Altitude Platform Station (HAPS) is a aerial node operating at an altitude of about 20 km in the stratosphere, allowing for longer flight times, wider coverage areas, and links for backhauling traffic from ground base stations. Driven by technological innovations in autonomous navigation, antenna arrays, artificial intelligence, and solar power supply, HAPS has become an important component of next-generation wireless networks. In this paper, we outline the key applications of HAPS constellations and the technical challenges for successful design and deployment of this technology. Subsequently, we leverage a line-of-sight probability predicated on the obstacle penetration rate in the first Fresnel zone, resulting in an analytical formulation for the LoS probability that is dependent on the operating frequency, the transmitter and receiver heights, the horizontal distance between them, and three additional parameters describing the statistical properties of the propagation environment. The model constructed is sufficiently accurate to capture scattering aspects such as reflectivity and diffusion, yet mathematically flexible enough to allow for a smooth and physically meaningful interpretation of the performance trend of advanced radio networks including HAPS.

articleTitle: Tuning the hyperparameters for supervised machine learning classification, to optimize detection of IoT Botnet
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: We all agreed that we are living in the Internet of Things (IoT) generation, pretty much any physical object that exists can transform into an IoT device if it can be connected or controlled to exchange information with a given network. That means in cybersecurity terms a lot of opportunities to create IoT botnets to break down the networks of these devices. Knowing that the majority of these devices are usually quite cheap, and of course, mass market-oriented, with no attention paid to access control, data protection, or any further security management. Consequently, they are immensely the favorite target for hackers to exploit their vulnerabilities to construct very many types of IoT botnets with different characteristics and goals, beginning by spying on a network to get control of all the other devices. For that, this paper comes to propose a study about how we can exploit the powerful benefits of supervised machine learning classification algorithms and models by tuning their hyperparameters, in order to regularize and minimize the measures of the error to get in last the best detecting of any type of these kinds of the botnet on a given network. This paper will combine two powerful innovations in computer science IoT and machine learning to give a hand of help on one of the most complicated fields in this science which is IoT network security by finding the answer of which is the favorable sets of hyperparameters that can be tuned in order to optimize the performance of detecting IoT botnet using some supervised machine learning classification models.

articleTitle: On the Latency and Complexity of Semi-Parallel Decoding Architectures for 5G NR Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Recently adopted in the New Radio (NR) standard for 5G control channel, polar codes represent one of the latest additions to the family of forward error correction (FEC) codes. However, the stringent requirements introduced by the 5G standard in terms of block length and code rate flexibility, together with low end-to-end latency and high error correction performance, pose a major challenge for their hardware implementation. In this context, we study the impact of main code and decoder design parameters on the latency and the hardware complexity of semi-parallel decoding architectures. Detailed analytical and logic synthesis results are provided and compared for a large range of values in order to constitute a reference for the implementation of flexible, yet efficient FEC decoders for polar codes.

articleTitle: Study of security problem in cloud computing with access control based on the blockchain
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Classic cloud data sharing systems are based on a network architecture and large storage providers. However, these providers are responsible for transferring and storing the data. This type of cloud storage model has some weaknesses, such as data availability, centralized data storage, high operational cost and security issues. In this paper, we study the security problem related to the data stored in the cloud by focusing on the use of blockchain combined with the attribute-based encryption (ABE) algorithm. The studied system meets the security requirements of the cloud, such as confidentiality and non-forgery. In addition, the smart contract solves the problem of cloud storage, such as the return of erroneous results as in the traditional cloud server.

articleTitle: Deployment Strategies of Mobile Networks for Internet-of-Things in Smart Maritime Ports
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: It is estimated that 80% of world trade is transported via maritime logistic. The maritime trade networks can be seen as a graph with links and nodes. For an optimal network, the links representing the maritime routes must be short (with minimal cost) and secure. The nodes of the network represents the maritime ports, which are hub sending, receiving or switching the goods (in form of containers). The ports has passed from analog to digital ports to make use of IT tools to speed up the process, especially the administrative part. Nowadays, we talk about smart ports that uses data to further speed up the process administratively but also use a full automation to accelerate/optimize the processing of the goods/containers in terminals/quay. Terminal Operation System (TOS) is the main components in these operations. Therefore, the use of Internet-of-Thing (IoT) in TOS a decisive step towards smart ports. In this work, we propose to extend the notion of IoT in other smart domains to be considered in the smart port paradigm, such smart building, smart grid, smart environment monitoring, etc. Furthermore, we study the optimal strategies for the deployment of a performing networking infrastructure, which is the core element in the IoT layered model. Private network based on Long Term Evolution (LTE/4G) has been estimated to be an optimal solution for private enterprise networking in Industry 4.0. Here, we analyze its suitability for smart maritime ports.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of the Whitening Methods in Linear Video Coding and Transmission Schemes
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Linear Video Coding and Transmission (LVCT) schemes, pioneered by the SoftCast architecture, have been recently proposed as an alternative solution for wireless broadcast applications where users may experience severe channel quality fluctuations. LVCT schemes offer a graceful video quality adaptation to the user experienced channel quality. This is made possible by relying on linear operators only (decorrelation transform, power allocation, whitening). The LVCT whitening process aims at reducing the impact of slice loss in presence of fades. It is mainly performed by Hadamard transform which is not adapted to all input sizes. Although alternatives to the Hadamard transform have been proposed in the literature, no performance comparison has been performed. In this paper, we compare the performance of SoftCast using three different whitening matrices, namely, Hadamard, Inverse Discrete Cosine Transform (IDCT) and Random matrices. Three scenarios are considered for the comparison: no packet loss, random packet losses and bursty packet losses. Simulation results confirm that these matrices offer similar reconstructed video quality in a lossless scenario, while whitening using a random orthogonal matrix outperforms whitening using Hadamard or IDCT matrices in all lossy scenarios.

articleTitle: Investigating generalization in automatic COVID-19 detection using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Computer Vision and Deep Learning have been widely used to automatically detect and analyze many diseases in various fields. Some of these include tumor detection, diabetic retinopathy classification, automatic prostate segmentation, nodules classification, etc. In this work, we are investigating the application of computer vision and deep learning techniques in COVID-19 detection from X-ray images. The general purpose was to offer an aided diagnosis system to assist radiologists in COVID-19 detection or to present a preliminary assessment when a radiologist is not immediately available. To address the problem of dependence on training data, and given the nature of the task, we opted for a double evaluation of the developed models. The proposed system appears promising for the diagnosis of COVID19, showing potential results in two different datasets.

articleTitle: Stochastic modeling of hyperconnected mobile modular production problem
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The industry is increasingly dependent on research and development. Today’s markets face new challenges: product life cycles are getting short, and product variability is increasing. This results in variable and uncertain product demands in both time and space. Hyperconnected mobile modular production offers new opportunities. It allows manufacturers to use a variety of open facilities that offer the required conditions for their type of production, by setting up their containerized modular production equipment and produce close to the customers. It therefore allows intelligent and agile proactivity to efficiently and sustainably meet the demand of a highly variable market. In this paper, we consider the problem of hyperconnected mobile modular production with demand uncertainty. We address the integrated optimization of distribution and production costs related to the usage of a network of hyperconnected facilities for responding to the dynamics of demand. To account for demand uncertainty, we propose a stochastic and resilient mixed integer programming formulation. Two forms of decision variables are used. binary variables for the selection of modular units and available open sites, and continuous variables for production scheduling. To deal with demand variability, a scenario method is applied. The objective function of our robust optimization model has two components: total expected costs and cost variability related to demand uncertainty.

articleTitle: Impact of regularization on the effectiveness of transfer learning for olive disease classification
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Transfer learning is a machine learning method where a model developed for a task is reused as the starting point for a model on a second task. This work presents an approach based on transfer learning associated with the regularization technique, as well as the data collection of olive diseases dataset (ODD) elaborated by authors. The results obtained are very promising and show the interest of transfer learning based on regularization, especially since the method makes it possible to overcome the constraint of having a large amount of data, in this perspective the proposed Mobile Net model held up particularly well to produce better results compared to other models under the same conditions.

articleTitle: The Impact of Forecasting Horizon and Resolution on PV Power Prediction using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Solar energy forecasting becomes a necessity in order to balance the supply and demand of this energy, therefore promote its planning, transmission and distribution. This work clarifies the impact of forecast horizon and resolution on model accuracy by exploiting the power of the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, which manages the shape of multidimensional data to embed small resolution in the input data. Four forecasting horizons were assessed (1 day, 1 hour, 15 minutes and 5 minutes) using Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model and three forecasting horizons (1 day, 1 hour and 15 minutes) were used within LSTM model to predict Photovoltaic (PV) power generated from 11 PV panels located in Eugene university, Oregon. The findings of this study indicate that in short term forecasting horizon, generally, the more the horizon decreases the more accurate the model becomes, as well as small data resolution is recommended.

articleTitle: Enhancing 5G Forward Error Correction Codes for URLLC by Spatial Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate how to relax the tradeoff between reliability and latency in 5G Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communications (URLLC) services. We propose a redesign of the 5G Forward Error Correction (FEC) code to increase its error correction capability for 5G-enabled URLLC use cases. Starting from the base matrix of the 5G standard Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) code we construct a spatially coupled base matrix. From this base matrix, a binary spatially coupled parity check matrix is then obtained after a lifting operation based on one of the lifting factors supported by the standard. The results of the simulation demonstrate that the proposing spatially-coupled codes allow additional coding gains of up to 0.8 dB under the considerate scenarios.

articleTitle: Relevant pitch features selection for voice disorders families classification
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Identification of voice disorders plays a major role in our life nowadays. In this context, voice analysis can be used, as a complementary technique with other traditional invasive methods, such as laryngoscopy, to identify voice disorders. This paper explores a set of acoustic features extracted from the vocal folds signals namely the pitch, to this purpose. First, 49 pitch-based features are extracted from speech recordings. Then, relevant ones are selected according to their discriminatory power between normal and pathological voice classes. To do so, different feature selection techniques have been used and compared. Afterward, KNN, SVM, Random Tree and Naive Bayes classifiers are applied to decide on the existence of a voice disorder or not and which pathological class is detected. The experimental results denote the usefulness of retained features and despite, the simplicity of classification technique (KNN for instance), the best performance in term of accuracy rate reached 91.5%.

articleTitle: On the use of Bayer Sensor Color Cameras in Digital Image Correlation
publicationTitle: 2022 11th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The digital image correlation (DIC) technique uses monochrome images, which are usually captured using monochrome cameras. Color cameras with Bayer filter patterns are available with higher specs and lower prices than monochrome cameras, and their images can be used in DIC after they are converted to monochrome. In this paper, in-plane rigid-body-translation experiments are used to compare the DIC strain measurement error for monochrome and color cameras under similar conditions. Furthermore, different algorithms for converting color images to monochrome are compared with the aim of reducing the DIC measurement error. The results show that monochrome images captured by color cameras cannot give the same level of accuracy as the images of monochrome cameras; however, DIC accuracy is dependent on the algorithm used for converting color-to-monochrome images. The results show that the interpolation methods used for demosaicing the color channels affect the DIC accuracy. For high contrast images, higher accuracy is achieved using low-order interpolation; while for low contrast images, higher-order interpolation gives better results. Interestingly, it is found that, for high contrast images, using the green channel image alone can give better DIC accuracy than the monochrome image that is obtained by combining the three channels.
